rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for something having a pleasantly high temperature.

example.english: The tea is still warm and best drunk right away.
example.jyutping: bui1 caa4 zung6 nyun5 ngaam1 ngaam1 jam2 zeoi3 hou2

rows.note: Use this as the default physical verb when making or keeping someone or something warm.

example.jyutping: gin6 lau1 ho2 ji5 nyun5 zyu6 nei5

rows.note: Use this when something becomes warm again or warms up after being cold.

example.english: The soup got cold, but it will warm up again after heating for a while.
example.traditional: 啲湯凍咗，翻熱一陣就暖返喇。
example.jyutping: di1 tong1 dung3 zo2 faan1 jit6 jat1 zan6 zau6 nyun5 faan1 laa3

rows.note: Use this for a person, manner, or relationship that feels friendly and affectionate.

example.english: They are very warm to people and will say hello first even when meeting someone for the first time.
example.traditional: 佢待人好親切，第一次見面都會主動打招呼。
example.jyutping: keoi5 doi6 jan4 hou2 can1 cit3 dai6 jat1 ci3 gin3 min6 dou1 wui5 zyu2 dung6 daa2 ziu1 fu1

rows.note: Use this for gradually becoming willing to accept an idea or proposal.

example.english: They began to warm to the proposal.
example.traditional: 佢哋聽完個建議，慢慢接受咗。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 teng1 jyun4 go3 gin3 ji5 maan6 maan6 zip3 sau6 zo2

rows.note: Use this specifically for colors in the red-to-yellow range or a warm-toned color scheme.

example.english: The living room uses warm colors as its main palette, so it feels much more comfortable.
example.traditional: 客廳用暖色做主調，感覺舒服好多。
example.jyutping: haak3 teng1 jung6 nyun5 sik1 zou6 zyu2 diu6 gam2 gok3 syu1 fuk6 hou2 do1

rows.note: Use this when a guess or answer is getting closer to the goal or correct answer.

example.english: You guessed thirty? You’re getting warm—the answer is thirty-two.
example.traditional: 你估三十？近喇，答案係三十二。
example.jyutping: nei5 gu2 saam1 sap6 gan6 laa3 daap3 on3 hai6 saam1 sap6 ji6
